chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about a man who was immoral with a woman; can he marry her mother from breastfeeding, or her daughter? He said: No.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — similar to it.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two; a reference to either the 5th or 6th Imam (peace be upon them) depending on the narrator chain.
key_terms.الرَّضَاعَةِ: Breastfeeding; refers to the legal concept of radha' (milk kinship) which creates mahram relationships.
key_terms.فَجَرَ: To be immoral or commit fornication; here used to denote a relationship that creates prohibition.

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the mother or daughter of a woman he was immoral with?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that 'fujur' (often interpreted as sexual intercourse or sometimes just the act itself depending on the school of thought) establishes a permanent mahram relationship akin to marriage, prohibiting the man from marrying the woman's mother or daughter. The narration highlights the consensus among the Imams, as seen in the parallel reports from Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) and the other Imam, reinforcing the legal weight of this prohibition. This ruling is crucial for understanding lineage and marriage validity in cases where consummation may not have occurred or where the specific nature of the act is debated.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who was immoral with a woman, can he marry her mother from the breastfeeding, or her daughter?’
Heasws said: ‘No’. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, form Muhammad Bin Muslim, from Abu Ja’farasws – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a man who had committed sinful acts with a woman if he could marry her breastfeeding mother or daughter. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’
Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim a similar Hadith.”
